metadata.description: A logical partition — the third form of Machine (CLS-004, by form): an OS-bearing slice of a partitioned system (IBM Power via PowerVM and the HMC; IBM Z via PR/SM) that boots an image onto entitled processor capacity, memory and virtual I/O. It honours every Machine element and adds the partitioning vocabulary no VM or bare-metal host has: fractional processor entitlement, capped or uncapped sharing, a shared processor pool, VIOS-backed virtual adapters. Names follow the HMC vocabulary; dialects (PowerVM, PR/SM) are the Provider tier.

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small | medium | large, ordered and comparable; common-elements §2.2). Sizes the machine in place of explicit cpu and memory; the provider maps the class to concrete resources at realization. A machine may be declared by size class alone.

count.description: Total virtual CPUs. The provider naturalizes this to its native cpu model (a KubeVirt domain cpu, a hypervisor platform's sockets*cores, a public cloud's vCPUs) at realization (DCM ADR-023).

sockets.description: Optional topology hint: sockets. Provider-support-dependent; ignored where not applicable.

cores_per_socket.description: Optional topology hint: cores per socket. Provider-support-dependent.

cpu.description: CPU requirement: `count` is the virtual CPUs the OS sees; sockets and cores per socket are optional topology hints. The provider maps it to its native model (hypervisor sockets×cores, cloud vCPUs).

size.description: Memory allocation, e.g. 16GB or 16Gi (class-aligned quantity pattern — Machine Base Class `memory.size`).

hugepages.description: Optional huge-page backing (provider-support-dependent; validated against provider capability).

memory.description: Memory requirement: `size` as a quantity (16Gi); `hugepages` optional.

storage.description: Numeric storage requirements the realizing storage must meet — IOPS, throughput, replication, encryption. The performance class is the governed `storage_tier` element, not a value here.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a governed `storage_tier` term (standard | performance | archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036): a tier name resolves to its floor, explicit `storage` requirements win where both are given, and any provider class that clears the floor qualifies. The provider records the native class it chose as a realized output. Profile decides whether a bare term or a data_reference is required. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

guest_os.description: The requested operating system. Portable form: a data_reference to an `os_image` term the provider advertises. Inline `{type, version}` is the portability-breaking escape. Optional: a machine may be declared by sizing alone; a profile may require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

entitled_capacity.description: Entitled processing units (fractions of a physical core; PowerVM minimum 0.05 per virtual processor).

sharing_mode.description: Dedicated cores, or shared capacity that is capped at the entitlement or may exceed it when the pool has headroom.

uncapped_weight.description: Priority for excess pool capacity; meaningful only with sharing_mode uncapped.

shared_pool.description: The shared processor pool the partition draws from, as the provider names it.

processor.description: Processor entitlement for the partition (HMC partition-profile settings): how much physical capacity it is entitled to and how it shares. `cpu.count`, inherited, is the virtual processors the OS sees.

vios_backed.description: Storage and network are served through Virtual I/O Servers rather than dedicated adapters.

virtual_io.description: Virtual I/O the partition is served through: VIOS-backed virtual SCSI, NPIV fibre channel, virtual or SR-IOV network adapters. A requirement the provider satisfies from its VIOS pair, never a reference to a registered device.

run_state.description: Desired partition run state the provider drives to (HMC activate / shut down). Distinct from the four-state lifecycle.

provider_handle.description: The provider-native partition name (opaque; correlation only).

primary_ip.description: The primary or management address of the booted machine — the single address most bindings want. Promoted from Machine.VM: a bare-metal host and an LPAR have one once booted.

hostname.description: Realized hostname (FQDN where the realm provides one). Promoted from Machine.VM.

partition_id.description: The partition identifier the managing system assigned.

observed_run_state.description: Observed partition state as the provider reports it.

relationships.description: The partitioned system (the frame or CEC) the partition runs on — a managed bare-metal host.

adopts.role: Vendor-neutral compute-system representation spanning physical, virtual and partitioned (Redfish ComputerSystem SystemType: Physical | Virtual | Composed | PhysicallyPartitioned | VirtuallyPartitioned) — the one representative standard for the Machine family, shared by Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost and Machine.LPAR and declared once here. Nova with Ironic, Cluster API's Machine and TOSCA's Compute are the industry abstractions that treat the three forms as one thing (CLS-002 (a)); Redfish is the wire representation adopted. Provider-native realizations are declared on the provider support matrix, not on the substrate type.

context.purpose: Declares a logical partition on a partitioned system as one provisionable Machine.
context.plain_description: The request for a slice of a big partitioned server: how much processor capacity it is entitled to and whether it may borrow more, how much memory, which image, and how its disks and network are served. The provider (an HMC-managed Power system, a PR/SM-managed mainframe) activates the partition and reports its identifier and state.
use_when: You need an OS instance on a partitioned system and want to state entitlement rather than pick a frame.
You are rebuilding an estate whose workloads run on Power or Z and need those hosts in the same graph as VMs and bare metal.
not_for: A VM on a hypervisor — that is Machine.VM.
The partitioned system itself — that is Machine.BareMetalHost; the partition is contained_by it.
works_with: Machine.BareMetalHost — the frame that hosts the partition.
Volume — the disks served through virtual I/O.
VirtualNetwork — the network a virtual adapter attaches to.
